thread:
Asha (Customer Success): FYI — FinBank reported a regression on the /v1/rerank endpoint after yesterday's model rollout. They claim identical input sets now produce different ranks and scores compared to pre-rollout. They're blocking a release. :rotating_light:

Priya (Support): Copying the report below from their ticket. They provided a minimal repro and screenshots. They said there were no schema changes on their side.

Asha (Customer Success): Repro summary from FinBank (pasted):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, Model: redwood-rerank-v3.2
Body: {
  "queries": ["invoice dispute policy", "how to dispute a charge"],
  "candidates": ["Doc A text...", "Doc B text...", "Doc C text..."]
}
```
Expected top score: Candidate B, score ~0.91 (old model v3.1). After v3.2 deploy: Candidate A top, score 0.63, B 0.57. They provided full JSON diffs.

Asha (Customer Success): They attached two saved request/response pairs (pre and post). I'm attaching their examples inline.

Priya (Support): Can you paste the exact responses here so we can compare?

Asha (Customer Success): Pre-rollout response (v3.1):
```
{"scores":[{"id":"A","score":0.72},{"id":"B","score":0.91},{"id":"C","score":0.44}]}
```
Post-rollout (v3.2):
```
{"scores":[{"id":"A","score":0.83},{"id":"B","score":0.57},{"id":"C","score":0.39}]}
```

Liam (ML Eng): Hmm — those are significant rank flips. Two quick questions: 1) were both calls pinned to same model hash? 2) any different query preprocessing (truncation, tokenization) on client side?

Asha (Customer Success): They claim same request body. Both requests show header Model: redwood-rerank-v3.1 and redwood-rerank-v3.2 respectively. No client-side changes.

Tom (Runtime): Deploy-bot log shows v3.2 rollout to hosted cluster at 2026-03-04T14:12Z. @deploy-bot, can you paste the rollout artifacts?

deploy-bot: Rollout completed. Artifact: rerank-model-redwood-rerank-v3.2 (sha: 3f6a9c). Canary 10% -> 100% over 18 minutes. No infra errors reported.

Liam (ML Eng): Thanks. Next: need to reproduce locally. Priya — can you ask FinBank for exact raw bytes of request (curl with -v) and the response bodies including response headers (x-model-hash, x-embed-latency, x-serving-node)? Also ask for an old pre-rollout exemplar if they still have it.

Priya (Support): On it. Sent request for raw captures and full headers.

Elena (Product): Also flagging this to prioritization — if this is a quality regression we may need a rollback or mitigation (canary config, fallback to v3.1 for that tenant).

Liam (ML Eng): I'll run a differential evaluation on the same input set across v3.1 and v3.2. Looking for pattern — is it structural (reweighting of signals) or bug (tokenization mismatch, loss scaling). Can take a few hours.

Tom (Runtime): A few notes on platform differences: v3.2 introduced a quantization fallback on certain sequence lengths to improve throughput. If the client's inputs hit that codepath, scores might shift slightly. We generally expect small deltas but not rank inversions like that. I'll check whether rerank pipeline accidentally toggled a fallback for all sequences.

Asha (Customer Success): FinBank just replied with curl dumps. They included an extra newline in candidates between entries for the pre-rollout test (they claim). I copied their exact curl for both cases.

Priya (Support): Paste of their post-rollout curl (as sent):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Model: redwood-rerank-v3.2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queries":["invoice dispute policy","how to dispute a charge"],"candidates":["Doc A text...","Doc B text...","Doc C text..."]}'
```
They included the same payload for pre-rollout but Model header was v3.1. No extra newlines in the -d body according to the curl dump.

Liam (ML Eng): OK. I ran their exact payload through our internal v3.1 and v3.2 binaries with the same seed/env. Reproduction results: v3.1 -> B top (0.905), v3.2 -> A top (0.827). So it's not just a client-side issue.

Tom (Runtime): Do you have the model hashes for both runs? Need to verify config flags and kernel selection.

Liam (ML Eng): v3.1 sha: b1c2d3, v3.2 sha: 3f6a9c. I also captured logits and attention weight summaries for the two runs; there is a noticeable re-scaling in final softmax inputs for B vs A.

Liam (ML Eng): Hypothesis 1: model architecture change or training objective tweak between v3.1 and v3.2 increased affinity to lexical overlap leading to A scoring higher. Hypothesis 2: quantization path in runtime introduced numerical differences concentrating mass on different candidates. Need ablations.

Elena (Product): From a product POV, we need a mitigation for FinBank ASAP — can we route their tenant to v3.1 until we confirm?

Tom (Runtime): Yes — we can pin their tenant to v3.1 via routing policy. Priya, can you provide the tenant ID?

Priya (Support): Tenant ID in ticket: finbank-prod-3. I set a temporary pin to v3.1 on their account and confirmed with deploy logs that traffic now targets v3.1. They verified that results now match old behavior. :white_check_mark:

Asha (Customer Success): FinBank is relieved but wants root cause and whether this could affect other customers. Also asked about SLAs and a postmortem.

Liam (ML Eng): Next steps I'm taking: 1) run batch evaluation across 10k representative queries between v3.1 and v3.2 to quantify rank-flip rates; 2) rerun v3.2 with quantization disabled to isolate runtime effects; 3) compare tokenization outputs for the candidate texts (just to be safe). I'll post findings here.

Tom (Runtime): I'll grep the rollout diff for any config flag that toggles quantization per-seq-len. Also checking whether GPU kernel fallback happened for this customer's shard at rollout time.

Priya (Support): FinBank asked if billing impact is possible (they saw slightly different token counts). I explained pinning won't affect billing for completed calls but asked finance to confirm any invoice-side concerns.

Elena (Product): We should prepare a customer-facing note: 1) acknowledgment, 2) mitigation performed, 3) expected next steps and ETA for root cause. Priya/Asha can draft; I'll review.

Liam (ML Eng): Quick update after initial ablation (2h): disabling quantization in v3.2 reduces magnitude of score shifts but doesn't fully restore v3.1 ordering. So it's likely a combination: model update + runtime quantization amplifies drift.

Tom (Runtime): Confirmed in logs that a quantization fallback was enabled by default for sequences under 64 tokens in the new runtime config. The candidate texts here are ~45-60 tokens, so they hit the codepath. I'll open a PR to revert the default and add a safety check to avoid large ranking deltas when fallback is in effect.

Liam (ML Eng): I'll create a patch to produce deterministic quantized posteriors (match fp32 where possible) and run a regression test. If we can reproducibly show the model change alone causes some flips but combined with quantization it's worse, we can justify a minor rollback of runtime default while keeping model rollout.

Asha (Customer Success): FinBank asked for a timeline. What's realistic for mitigation and root cause report?

Tom (Runtime): Revert PR for runtime default in 2-4 hours (hotfix).

Liam (ML Eng): Regression numbers and a writeup in 24 hours. If we need a full model rollback, product and infra will decide.

Elena (Product): Good. Priya/Asha — draft customer note and send to FinBank with pin details and ETA 24h. Keep me in cc.

Priya (Support): Done — message sent and FinBank acknowledged. They request a technical postmortem once root cause is confirmed.

Asha (Customer Success): Closing loop: pin remains in place until we confirm that v3.2 + runtime changes are safe. I'll update the ticket. Thanks everyone. :pray:

Liam (ML Eng): I'll post the 10k-eval summary here when ready.

Tom (Runtime): PR opened: revert-quant-defaults (#4829). Marking for emergency review.

Elena (Product): Adding this to the incident tracker for visibility.

(reacts :eyes:)
